title: Quantile-gated kernel selector and stream-smoothing admission
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Reduce P95/P99 tail latency for mixed short/long request workloads by combining a streaming-aware admission gate with a quantile tail estimator and dynamic kernel fit probing. This ticket implements: (1) a low-overhead online P99 estimator per-tenant that influences admission window size; (2) a lightweight kernel-probing mechanism that measures small-sample kernel throughput for the current attention shape and prefill distribution; (3) a stream-smoothing admission loop that decays admission aggressiveness for long-running streams to avoid tail amplification during decode bursts. The goal is to improve end-to-end P99 by at least 20% on our production tail incident pattern (short interactive bursts followed by long decodes), without increasing median latency more than 5% or lowering throughput for high-throughput tenants.
acceptance_criteria: P99 end-to-end latency reduction >= 20% on recorded burst traces compared to baseline (runtime-1.18).
Median latency increase <= 5% on stable steady-state traffic.
No regression in token throughput for dedicated customers in nightly perf tests (±1%).
Feature gated behind runtime-1.19 flag and configurable per-customer in console.
Automated unit + integration tests for estimator, probe, and admission FSM merged into CI.
implementation_notes: Estimator: use an exponential-weighted quantile sketch (error bounds tuned for p95/p99 range) to keep CPU + memory low; keep per-tenant state bounded by recent-window TTL.

Kernel probe: opportunistic single-shot microbench of candidate kernel for observed attention width and sequence lengths; cache probe results keyed by (model-arch, attention-width-bucket, quantized-seq-length).
Admission FSM: three states (Aggressive, Stabilize, Conservative); transition triggered by estimator crossing configurable quantile thresholds and by recent probe outcomes (fit/mismatch).
Prefill/Decode scheduling: when a stream enters Conservative state, prefer prefill coalescing and staggered decode slots (max 2 concurrent decodes per GPU per-tenant) to prevent tail queuing.
Telemetry: emit transition events, estimator quantiles, probe latencies, and kernel-choice reasons to improveability dashboard. Add tracing hooks for specific request IDs that triggered transitions.
Safety: feature defaults to disabled; enable via runtime flag runtime.batch.quantile_gated=true and per-customer override in console.
test_plan: Unit tests for quantile estimator correctness and TTL behavior.
Microbench harness: run kernel probes across model family matrix used in our catalog and verify cached entries are used on second call.
Integration: replay production burst traces in perf-cluster and compare P50/P95/P99 against baseline.
Chaos: run spike-and-slow-decode scenarios with fault-injected probe failures and ensure admissions degrade gracefully (fall back to Conservative without CPU error loops).
E2E Canary: enable feature for internal-dev tenants in runtime-1.19 canary; monitor dashboard for risk signals for 48h before broader rollout.
